restrictions: Target sha256-r37-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..36 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is verified with the target before it is returned.

Algorithm: the two-block attack of Li, Zhang, Li, Liu, Qian and Zhu (IACR ePrint 2026/1120) with its 37-step characteristic and the Step-1 solution S of its published SFS pair as transcribed in 6c77089c, the 222 largest classes of A0-variants of S (782,800 variants; 1c368173, b947b377, 1f12a09a), each class base | s for s in one of ten lists whose free bits 0, 2, 3 (or 0) form a cube (proof.md Sections 5.3, 8.1), and the packed good-pair stage of 0db0eeb6; as in ffbe30bb the eight value bits E18[1,5,10,11,18,28,29], E19[29] are not imposed (four patterns, Section 7.6); new here (R16x), E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] are not imposed (Section 7.4c). No x-indexed table and no row-16 mask table: per first block a bit-sliced W7 test of the 222 classes, per passing class bit-sliced W6 tests in at most 8 runs, the packed row-16 address, two 4096-word chunk tables and an exact test, then rows 16..21 by cells and rows 22..36 replayed with the eight registers compared (proof.md Sections 6.2, 7.4d, 8, 9).

Cost: fixed caps N_FB = 24650628322256370 first blocks (2^54.45247; each one target compression plus 615 counted operations) and V_MAX = 1135933807571123291014 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded), with A_C = 10,392,620,003 (3,686 CPU-seconds of a completed 8-seed search of the 37-step dense instance at 2^21.427 units per CPU-second: measured, H4), A_S = 2^50 (Step-1 re-solve, bounded by its caps, proof.md Section 11.2), DEV = 2^40 (development) and 2^38 operations of preprocessing (Section 14.2); the characteristic and the SFS pair are published (ePrint 2026/1120, Tables 15-17, in the package) and their construction is charged (A_C, A_S): 2^58.677978 target compressions on every run (Section 11), claimed 58.67798. Every target compression is charged one unit; every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition (address additions included), comparison and branch is one primitive, the plane programs counted by an algebra with static constants and inversion flags (Section 9.1).

Success probability at least 0.39 (0.3900000020) under H1 (independent uniform chaining values of the first blocks), H2 (q3 >= 2^-70.16 for the exact end event of rows 22..36 with the four row-18/19 value patterns and R16x accepted jointly: the cell-event bound 2^-71.4629 of two preregistered blocks of 128 replicates times the preregistered exact/cell ratio bound 2.4786, rounded down, proof.md Sections 7.4c, 7.4d, Appendices G, H.4, K; for H3 only, q3 <= 2^-70.06, Appendix H.4) and H3 (average of further successes in the same first block at most 2^-9.4) and H7, by a per-first-block Bonferroni bound and independence across first blocks; Chebyshev bounds the work-cap overflow (cap slack 2^-12, squared) below 0.00138975. No expected-work bound and no independence-of-conditions model is used.

Memory: 2^29 bytes (536,870,912), a declared bound (H6) over all phases including the construction of the characteristic (proof.md Appendix H.2): online tables, code and constants 607,744 bytes = 2^19.21 (computed); preprocessing below 2^27 bytes plus the tables (computed); the construction of the characteristic (generator, CNF dump, solver) under prlimit --as=536870912, largest measured peak 500,424,704 bytes = 2^28.899 (the STP CNF dump); its solver completed on that CNF in 8 seeds under prlimit --as=379625062; the Step-1 re-solve under prlimit --as=117440512 (measured peak 88,006,656 bytes); its completion in the organizer's 128 MB sandbox. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement. The per-first-block counts of the ledger are exact expectations or stated bounds on them (Section 11.1).

Nothing else in the claim is heuristic: the operation counts and the ledger (proof.md Sections 9, 11, Appendix B), the exactness of the filters F6, F7 and of the row-16 test (Section 13.2, Appendix A), the success arithmetic (Section 10, Appendix C) and the cap are computed or checked exhaustively; the premises are H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, H6 and H7 in claim.heuristics; A_S is bounded by the caps of its re-solve.

heuristics.statement: ASSUMPTION (no proof is known): The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings; their chaining values CV1 = F_37(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values; in particular x = A_{-1} is uniform on 2^32 and independent of cb = C6 - A_{-2}, which is uniform on 2^32. Consequences used: each of the 222 classes passes the W7 test with probability p7 = |F7|/2^32 exactly, each variant of a passing class then passes F6 with probability p6 = |F6|/2^32 exactly, and given both, W0..W5 are uniform and independent of (W6, W7) (proof.md Lemma 5.1); hence the expected number of good pairs per first block is g = 782,800 p7 p6 = 830.988, the expected counts of the ledger, and the independence of distinct first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected numbers of passing classes, good pairs, survivors and row-16 passes per first block; the expected operation count of the counted program; the law of the second-block words that defines q3; independence across first blocks (proof.md Section 10). Not the validity of any output: every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured by 7319bba with the attack's own filters on real first blocks in C (2^21 and 2^23 first blocks: passing classes 7,400,134 and 29,545,568 against 7,388,160 and 29,552,640 expected; good pairs ratio 1.0034 and 1.0011), by this filing's simulation of the counted program on 50,000 real first blocks (passing classes per first block 3.529 against the exact 3.523, good pairs 835.0 against 831.0), and in this refile by our own C program on 2,147,483,648 first blocks (2^31.0; proof.md Appendix H.6c): passing classes per first block 3.5229 against the exact 3.5229 and good pairs 831.0 against 831.0 (ratios 1.0000 and 1.0000, relative standard errors 0.0001 and 0.0001), top-byte buckets of x and of C6 - A_-2 within 0.0011 and 0.0011 of the mean. These are 2^31.0 real first blocks, not 2^58.3. Sensitivity (Appendix H.5; time_log2 that keeps 0.39, if the good-pair rate is (1 - eps) of g): eps = 0.01: 58.69244; 0.05: 58.75180; 0.10: 58.82963; 0.25: 59.09213. The organizer experiments a0-online-r37 (functional exactness) and h1-cv1-filters-nonce (filter pass rates on organizer-seeded blocks, counts not shown to the judge) are program checks and not evidence for H1 at scale.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption, not a theorem; measured on at most 2^31.0 first blocks against about 2^54.45 used. The class tests of one first block are strongly correlated (their c7 values are close), so per-first-block counts are overdispersed; only their expectations and the independence across first blocks are used. The class test uses the single word x, so H1 is also an assumption about that word of the digest of a 37-step compression. What the measurements cannot show: the joint law of x and cb beyond the two uniformity checks, independence of distinct blocks, or any tail event.

heuristics.statement: ASSUMPTION (no proof is known): For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 782,800 variants of the 222 classes (each equally likely, as examined here) and the 32 elements of L* of Pr[rows 16..21 of both members follow every cell and every printed two-bit condition closing at rows 16..21 (corrected reading A15[29] = A17[29]), the eight value bits E18[1,5,10,11,18,28,29] and E19[29] of Table 15 not imposed, and (R16x) E16[23] = 0 and E16[24] = E17[24] not imposed, and rows 22..36 replayed on the raw schedule words end with the eight registers of the two members equal: exactly the checks of experiments/lowm.py step3b] satisfies q3 >= q3_used = 2^-70.16 (the score uses only this) and q3 <= 2^-70.06 (used only by H3; derived in proof.md Appendix H.4), where 2^-70.16 is the sum, rounded down to two decimals of log2, of the 99 percent lower bound 2^-71.4629 of q3_cell (the same event with the cells of rows 22..36 imposed; the lower of the one-sided 99 percent Student lower bounds of the means of two preregistered blocks of 128 replicates, NP = 8192, of a sequential Monte-Carlo estimator written for this filing, Appendices F and G) and the 99 percent lower bound 2.4786 of the ratio q3 / q3_cell (preregistered, 2 x 128 seeds, pooled ratio 2.4848; proof.md Section 7.4d, Appendix K), run on exactly this family with both relaxations as one carrier.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g 32 q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10). The good pairs and the later rows are those of 7319bba; this filing changes how the good pairs are found, not which pairs are good, and which pairs count as a success: (from ffbe30bb) the value patterns of rows 18 and 19 and (new) R16x at rows 16 and 17, which also gives the four l = 0, 2, 16, 18 row-16 values.
heuristics.extrapolation: Lemma 7.1: rows 16..22 have exactly the same probability for every variant; a variant enters rows >= 23 only through W8 in W23 and W24, so only the four W24 conditions can depend on it (about 2^-4 for every W8x). Our estimator (exact row 16, exact importance weights at rows 17..21, (W6, W7) uniform on F6 x F7, W8 drawn uniformly from the 782,800 variants; Appendix F) was preregistered (validation V with Table 15 cells: mean 2^-73.9911, bound 2^-74.0064, z = +0.66 against the registered study B of 7319bba, mean 2^-73.9987, bound 2^-74.0225, validation PASSES both preregistered criteria (|z| <= 2.576; bound within 0.04 of -74.0225); main blocks R1 and R2 with the eight value characters of the two E cells removed: means 2^-71.9975 and 2^-71.9868, relative sd 0.0714 and 0.0681, bounds 2^-72.0191 and 2^-72.0074, declared 2^-72.02; stage factors of rows 18, 19 and 21 -8.00, -10.00 and -2.00 bits against -15.00, -6.00 and -1.00 for Table 15, structural gain 2.00) and again with R16x (constants written from the counted program; the same binary reproduces the four-pattern outputs byte for byte; joint blocks J1 and J2: means 2^-71.4296 and 2^-71.4177, relative sd 0.1096 and 0.1143, bounds 2^-71.4629 and 2^-71.4524, 0.55 bits above the four patterns alone; our earlier full-path test of R16x with independent rehash of all 30,814 collisions gave +0.590 bit [0.548, 0.631]). The four-pattern relaxation (exactly four feasible patterns, three verified further collisions) is ffbe30bb's; here the three collisions are re-checked against this package's cells. R16x is ours (each of its two conditions alone is necessary; a sweep of 30 further condition pairs found no further gain). Here the examined law is the studied law (every variant of every passing class, no weighting), so no hedge is added. Exact event (proof.md Section 7.4d, Appendix K): the program accepts a pair iff the cells of rows 16..21 hold and rows 22..36, replayed on the raw schedule words, end with the eight registers of both members equal. The ratio of exact to cell events over the same proposals was preregistered (2 x 128 seeds, rule fixed in advance) and measured 2.4870 and 2.4826 (pooled 2.4848, standard error 0.0027; cell_not_exact = 0; the same program on the 782,800 variants of the 222 classes only: 2.4738, standard error 0.0106); its lower bound 2.4786 (+1.3095 bit) gives q3_used = 2^-70.16 (the cell event: 2^-71.47). With q3 one bit lower the claim would be 59.67291, with the cell-event value 2^-71.47 59.98193, with the four patterns alone with cells (2^-72.02) 60.53062 and with the Table 15 value 2^-74.03 62.53851. Upper bound (Appendix H.4): the cell event has 99 percent Student upper bounds 2^-71.397 (J1) and 2^-71.384 (J2); times the 99 percent upper bound of the ratio, 2.4911, q3 <= 2^-70.06. Sensitivity (time_log2 that keeps 0.39 if q3 is 2^b below q3_used): b = 0.5: 59.17502; 1: 59.67291; 2: 60.67036; 4: 62.66845.
heuristics.limitations: A Monte-Carlo bound, not a theorem; its coverage rests on the approximate normality of the mean of 128 replicates (relative sd 0.1096 and 0.1143, about twice the Table 15 study's because few children survive the row-19 stage); row-22 survivors are heavily duplicated within a replicate; the row-22 stage draws (W6, W7) uniformly from F6 x F7, which is argued, not measured; depends on the reading of the '+' cells. The estimator is ours and was validated against the registered study, not against a second independent implementation. The count of four patterns is a solver enumeration (Bitwuzla; Z3 on smaller cases) for the published dense part with the signed cells of rows 14 and 15 kept (with rows 12..15 removed as well it admits 128 patterns); other dense parts were not explored, and our estimator does not use the solver. R16x has no solver enumeration: its value rests on the estimator and on our full-path test with rehashed collisions; patterns of rows 16..21 outside the program's cells (for example the E18 XOR pattern {24,23,16,15}) are not counted. No organizer experiment estimates q3. The ratio was measured with W8 drawn from the family G of 12,103,680 variants and checked on the 782,800 variants of this filing (2.4738, standard error 0.0106); the two bounds of the product come from different runs (coverage at least 98 percent by the union bound). A stated premise, not an established fact. The coverage of the Student bounds was checked against a percentile bootstrap (agreement to 0.001 bit, skewness 0.2 to 0.4) and not by a second independent estimator; the organizer experiments here do not estimate q3.

heuristics.statement: ASSUMPTION (no proof is known): the average over the trials t = (first block, variant, l), with the weights Pr[A_t], of the expected number of other successful trials of the same first block given that t succeeds is at most 2^-9.4: sum_t Pr[A_t] E[X_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-9.4 sum_t Pr[A_t]; this is all the Bonferroni sum of proof.md Section 10 uses, and we assume it for every t. Equivalently for every t: (a) the expected number of other l in L* succeeding with the same variant is at most 2^-11, and (b) for other good pairs t' of the same first block, Pr[t' succeeds | t succeeds, t' good] <= 2^35 Pr[t' succeeds | t' good].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= (1 - 2^-10.4) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10). The good pairs of a first block and their dependence structure are those of 7319bba; this filing changes the order in which they are processed, not the set.
heuristics.extrapolation: (a) 7319bba's replay of 19,620,436 distinct Step-3 successes of the SMC: rebuilding W0..W5 and testing the other 31 elements of L* through rows 14..36 gave 0 further successes (rule-of-three 95 percent bound 2^-22.65 per success; the accepted patterns raise the chance of passing rows 18 and 19 by about 4 and R16x the chance of the whole path by about 1.6, with four more l holding row 16, so about 2^-19.8, far below 2^-11; in that replay the other l fail at row 16 or 17). (b) With q3 <= 2^-70.06 (H2, the exact event; Appendix H.4), the expected number of further successes among other good pairs is at most rho x N_good x 32 x q3 with N_good <= 782,800 (all variants of the family): 2^35 x 2^19.58 x 2^5 x 2^-70.06 = 2^-10.48, so delta <= 2^-11 + 2^-10.48 = 2^-9.71 < 2^-9.4 (the break-even q3 is 2^-69.56); the measured factor at the row-16 level over 2^21 and 2^23 real first blocks is 0.98 and 1.00. This is the bound of the earlier filings on this family; the whole family G would give 2^-6.5 and is not used. For the cell event (q3_cell <= 2^-71.38) it would be delta <= 2^-11 + 2^-11.80 = 2^-10.34. Program check of this refile (Appendix H.6b, not a proof): over 1,173,546 first blocks (978,760,264 good pairs) the number of same-first-block pairs of distinct good pairs that both pass row 16 was 2,688,811 against 2677422 expected if the pairs were independent (ratio 1.00), and the later rows had row 17: 2 observed against 0.142 expected; row 18: 0 observed against 1.22e-05 expected. Sensitivity (time_log2 that keeps 0.39 for delta = 2^-9.4 (filed), 2^-8, 2^-6, 2^-4, 0.1, 0.25): 58.67798, 58.68254, 58.69958, 58.76980, 58.82856, 59.09107.
heuristics.limitations: An assumption, not a theorem. Rows >= 17 of distinct good pairs cannot be measured jointly at the claimed scale (the check of Appendix H.6b has too few events beyond row 17 to say anything); the premise leaves a margin of 2^35 over the measured row-16 factor, and the margin over the number of examined pairs is thin (delta <= 2^-9.71 with q3 <= 2^-70.06, against 2^-9.4: a margin of 0.31 bit). The replay samples of 7319bba are correlated through SMC resampling. The organizer experiment h3-cowpass-nonce is a W6-level program check whose counts the judge does not see.

heuristics.statement: The published characteristic, its two-bit conditions, the SFS pair's inner values S and L* are used as advice, and their construction is charged (collision-frontier-v5: "All construction/preprocessing and advice must be accounted for, including any search omitted from the submitted program"). A_S = 2^50 (the Step-1 SAT solve, reported by the paper at 2^41.3, and the completion of a Step-1 solution to the SFS pair) and A_C = 10,392,620,003 units = 2^33.275 (measured: a completed 8-seed kissat search of the real 37-step dense instance, 3,686 solver CPU-seconds at the price of 6eeefb64; proof.md Appendix L); all development computation at DEV = 2^40. The variant family, the 222 class descriptors (below 2^13 bytes), the lists, the filter sets, L* and the tables are recomputed in the preprocessing (2^38 operations bound, itemised in proof.md Section 14.2).
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (2^50.00142) and the advice (below 2^13 bytes).
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 11.2 and Appendices H.3 and L. A_S: 2^8.7 times the paper's reported Step-1 cost; the completion of a Step-1 solution to a full 37-step semi-free-start pair is reproduced in this package in about 25 milliseconds per pair (organizer experiment a0-sfs-r37). A_C: eight kissat 4.0.4 seeds on the CNF of the dense model (sha256 445a880e...42f4) all returned SATISFIABLE, the first after 457.01 s; the portfolio is charged 8 x 457.01 + 29.45 (setup) = 3,685.53, rounded up to 3,686 CPU-seconds, at the CPU-second price calibrated in the accepted filing 6eeefb64 (2^21.427 units at C = 2644); every model satisfies all clauses and decodes to a valid dense characteristic.
heuristics.limitations: A_C is the cost of the search we ran, on the dense instance with rows 16..24 and W22, W24 fixed to the published cells; its characteristic differs from the published one in rows 6..15; it is not the paper's own search, whose time is unpublished. The premise is that this completed search bounds the cost of constructing the characteristic the program uses (it replaces the earlier premise that the authors' search was no cheaper than 2^60). The price per CPU-second was calibrated on another machine and solver and our cloud CPU was not compared with it. Sensitivity: the claim is unchanged at five decimals up to A_C = 2^36 units, 58.67799 at 2^40, 58.68150 at 2^50, 60.48540 at 2^60 (the allowance of d0789558).

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5 a word-RAM program of 256-bit primitives in which every executed load, store, logic operation, shift, addition, comparison, branch and jump is one primitive is charged by the primitives it executes. The W7 class test (166 primitives for all 222 classes) and the W6 test of a batch of 256 reps (404 to 431 primitives, and 88 to 95 for each subtraction run) are straight-line plane programs whose counts do not depend on the data, produced by a plane algebra in which static constants fold and complemented planes carry an inversion flag at no cost, and in which a NOT is paid when an AND or OR meets unequal flags; two batches are processed together bit by bit with at most 20 live planes each (64 registers, no spill). The group of four members is 31 primitives, the probe of a lane 11 or 12, the exact row-16 test 34, with the scalar and control items of proof.md Section 9. The online tables, the code (bounded by 2^16 bytes) and the constants occupy 607,744 bytes = 2^19.21; the claimed memory is 2^29 bytes, the declared bound H6 over all phases including the construction of the characteristic (proof.md Section 14.1 and Appendix H.2). The 222 classes are base | s for s in ten lists (computed, checked for all 782,800 variants); a list is the union of 2^|B| translates of its reps by the cube B of free bits {0, 2, 3} or {0}, and W6x does not depend on a cube bit s_b when q_b = 1 (Lemma 8.2: proved from the constants of S and checked), which the program uses to run only the main combination and subtract the constants of the other 2^|Q0| - 1 combinations that matter.
heuristics.scope: The class-test, W6, scan, gather, group, probe and survivor terms of the ledger (essentially all of the 46070.09 data-dependent operations per first block), the fixed terms, the memory figure and the preprocessing bound (2^38 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: The program is experiments/lowm.py (the plane programs assert their counts at every execution; process_cv counts every scalar item where it executes; the realized operation count of every category equals its closed formula on 50,000 simulated first blocks). It is exact against the scalar definitions: every lane of every class-test plane and every pass plane equals the F7 or F6 test of its definition (44,400 and 42,972 lanes in selftest, and every lane of every processed class in a0-online-r37), the sets of good pairs (all members, after the expansion of the reps) equal the brute-force sets, the address u equals W0 + s0(W1) from the step equations, the exact row-16 test equals the exhaustive enumeration of 2,097,152 pairs on all 32 l under the row-16 parity relaxation (Appendix A) and the generic row check on random and near-miss values, and the table stage never rejects a member.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited for the plane algebra (static constants and inversion flags are compile-time facts of the text; the W6 programs have 81 to 82 inversion flips that cost nothing because XORs absorb them and AND/OR of equally flagged planes use De Morgan; pricing every one of them as a NOT would give about 58.7198) or for the register argument, which is a count of live planes, not a register allocation. The code size is a bound (at most 8192 primitives of at most 8 bytes). Branch pricing follows the earlier filings (a branch on a register is one primitive). The ceiling of the group count and the survivor scan are charged at their worst case (below 0.2 percent of the data-dependent work).

heuristics.statement: ASSUMPTION (a declared bound, enforced by an address-space cap): the peak memory of the whole procedure, the online program, the construction of the characteristic (the generation of the SAT instance of the 37-step dense model, its CNF dump and the solver search, charged as A_C), the Step-1 solve and its completion, development and the preprocessing, is at most 2^29 = 536,870,912 bytes, so memory_log2_bytes = 29 and the score is time_log2 + 9. The online tables, code and constants take 607,744 bytes = 2^19.21.
heuristics.scope: The memory term of the score. The time ledger is unchanged. The bound covers the phases that charge A_C, A_S and DEV, including the construction of the characteristic, whose solver search was completed in 8 seeds under a 2^28.5 address-space cap.
heuristics.extrapolation: Measured peaks (resident set, one thread, our machine, not run by the organizer; proof.md Appendix H.2): generator gen37.py 98,352 KB, translation to SMT2 97,360 KB, STP 2.4.1 CNF dump (200,534 variables, 954,732 clauses; sha256 445a880e...42f4) 487,680 KB = 499,384,320 bytes (2^28.895), each run under prlimit --as=536870912 and reproducing the earlier outputs byte for byte; kissat 4.0.3 on that CNF under an address-space cap of 2^28: zero-conflict peak 157,622,272 bytes (2^27.232) and, in three seeds run to 2^22 conflicts, an address-space peak of at most 2^27.790; kissat 4.0.4, 8 seeds run to completion on that CNF under prlimit --as=379625062 (2^28.5), maximum resident set at most 83,820,544 bytes (2^26.32), and the same STP dump on the cloud at 500,424,704 bytes (2^28.899); the Step-1 solve and the other stand-ins at most 2^27.569; online 607,744 bytes. Logs: premise_tests/P12/ and premise_tests/P12/logs_zf5/. Sensitivity (score = time_log2 + log2(peak) - 20): declared 2^29: 67.67798 (claimed); largest measured 2^28.899: 67.58.
heuristics.limitations: A declared bound, not a theorem. The solver search of the dense instance was observed to completion (8 seeds) under a cap of 2^28.5; we did not run the paper's own search. The cap ends any run that would exceed it, and then the construction fails. The STP dump alone needs 2^28.899 bytes, so a bound of 2^28 would not hold. The measurements are single runs on one local machine.

heuristics.statement: The cap target is mu0 = 0.49694499, the smallest 8-decimal number strictly above -ln(0.61 - Pcap - 2^-60) / (1 - 2^-10.4) with Pcap = 0.00138975 the assumed bound of the Chebyshev work-cap failure probability. With E[X] >= mu0 the success bound of proof.md Section 10, 1 - exp(-(1 - 2^-10.4) mu0) - Pcap - 2^-60, is >= 0.39000000 with no further padding.
heuristics.extrapolation: Every allowance is an explicit term of the floor equation: the Chebyshev cap-failure bound Pcap (priced in proof.md Section 10 from the exact vmax_fb and vbar of the ledger; the computed bound is 2^-9.49), the repeated-first-block allowance 2^-60, and the H3 dependence discount as the divisor (1 - 2^-10.4). Appendix C computes mu0 and the bound with 60-digit decimals and asserts the bound > 0.39; lowm.py ledger() iterates Pcap and N_FB to a fixed point and asserts the same.
heuristics.limitations: The 0.39 floor is the organizer's success requirement; the equation makes the success arithmetic exact rather than adding slack.
